articles.title: PM Modi, Nepal PM Balendra Shah to meet on November 23; new air routes, economic aid on agenda
articles.summary: New Delhi: Kathmandu’s proposal for a $2-billion economic assistance package from New Delhi and its long-standing demand for additional routes for international flights entering Nepal through the airspace of India, including the vexed issue of making the L626 corridor bidirectional, are likely to figure in the talks between the prime ministers of the two countries on Monday. India may, in principle, agree to Nepal’s proposal for the economic assistance package but is likely to insist on phased disbursement linked to specific projects. The package is expected to include around $500 million as a grant for reconstruction and rehabilitation in areas devastated by the August 26 flash floods, which caused extensive damage along Nepal’s border with the Tibet Autonomous Region of China. The remaining amount is likely to comprise a concessional loan of $1 billion and a $500 million grant for upgrading the Siddhartha Highway, connecting India to Pokhara in central Nepal. New Delhi may also agree on allowing more routes through its airspace for commercial passenger and cargo planes to fly in and out of Nepal but is likely to ask Kathmandu for reciprocal arrangement for aircraft using the airspace of Nepal to fly to and from the airport in Bagdogra in the northern region of West Bengal of India. Nepal PM Balen Shah arrives in Delhi for first bilateral visit, to hold talks with PM Modi on Monday Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to host his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah at Hyderabad House in New Delhi for the first meeting between the two leaders. The meeting is likely to result in several agreements and announcements covering development partnership, energy, hydropower, railways and connectivity, besides expanding bilateral cooperation in climate change, disaster resilience, infrastructure and technology. A few hours after Balendra Shah arrived in New Delhi on Sunday for his first visit to India after taking over as the prime minister of Nepal on March 27 this year, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar called on him. “India cherishes the special friendship with Nepal,” Jaishankar posted on X after meeting Shah. Apart from meeting Modi, Shah will also call on President Droupadi Murmu before his departure to Kathmandu on Monday. The two prime ministers are likely to discuss Kathmandu’s demand for New Delhi to allow three additional routes through the airspace of India for passenger and cargo aircraft to enter Nepal using Janakpur, Bhairahawa and Nepalgunj entry points. Nepal has been pressing India for improving viability of its new international airports at Pokhara and Bhairahawa, both constructed by state-owned companies of China. For Kathmandu, securing more air entry points through the airspace of India is crucial to shortening the circuitous flight paths that international carriers now must follow to reach Nepal. Most international flights at present enter Nepal at Simara in southcentral region of the country after flying through India, forcing the aircraft approaching from the west to take a significantly long detour. Nepal has been pressing for access through western entry points to cut flying time and fuel costs and improve the commercial prospects of the Bhairahawa and Pokhara international airports, which were inaugurated in 2022 and 2023, respectively. New Delhi has been concerned over China’s persistent bid to spread its geopolitical influence over Nepal and build strategic assets in the country, not only elbowing out but also posing a security threat to India. India-Nepal ties need a reset; Balendra Shah's visit could be the moment The two new airports were envisaged as Nepal’s second and third international gateways after Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu. However, both have struggled to attract sustained international air traffic. While Pokhara has recently secured a scheduled Dubai service operated by Flydubai, Bhairahawa continues to remain without regular international passenger flights. The limited air connectivity has raised questions about the commercial viability of the two major infrastructure investments. Modi and Shah are also likely to discuss Nepal’s long-pending request to India to make the L626 air corridor bidirectional. The route through the airspace of India has been available to international flights leaving Nepal since November 19, 2009. India, however, has not been allowing aircraft to use it to enter Nepal. Kathmandu wants the restriction lifted to enable two-way traffic. But the two sides, according to diplomatic sources, have differences over the altitude at which inbound flights could use the corridor, with New Delhi proposing 39,000 feet against Kathmandu’s preference for around 29,000 feet. India has been cautious about giving its nod to Nepal’s request for the additional western routes through Bhairahawa and Nepalgunj, particularly because of their proximity to the Indian Air Force’s strategically important base in Gorakhpur in Uttar Pradesh. With the IAF using the base for fighter aircraft operations and exercises, India has been reluctant to permit civilian flights to fly at lower altitudes to enter Nepal through the three proposed new routes, citing the need to safeguard sensitive military installations and manage airspace used for defence operations. The discussions the two prime ministers on Monday are also expected to touch upon reciprocal access to airspace, with New Delhi seeking Kathmandu’s permission for civilian aircraft to use the airspace of Nepal while flying to and from Bagdogra airport in West Bengal in India. Kathmandu has indicated its willingness to consider New Delhi’s proposal, subject to technical study. New Delhi, however, may insist on a firm commitment from Kathmandu, sources told DH . Shah, an alumnus of Visvesvaraya Technological University in Karnataka , led the Rashtriya Swatantra Party to a landslide victory in parliamentary elections in Nepal in March, riding the wave of aspirations triggered by the Gen Z uprising, which had, in September 2025, swept Nepal and overthrown the government led by K P Sharma Oli of the Communist Party of Nepal (United Marxist-Leninist) or CPN-UML. Though Shah had used the ‘F’ word for both India and China in a late-night social media post in November 2025, New Delhi reached out to him, and Modi extended an invitation to him.

articles.title: India, Iran hold bilateral meet; no formal talks with Pakistan on sidelines of SCO forum
articles.summary: New Delhi: India and Iran held bilateral talks on the sidelines of the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum to bolster cultural cooperation, Union Culture Secretary Vivek Aggarwal said on Sunday. At a press interaction held at the venue, the historic Purana Quila, shortly before the closure of the session, asked if any formal bilateral talks were held between India and Pakistan on the sidelines, Aggarwal said, "There were no formal bilateral talks between the two sides." However, he said that members of the Indian side did have interactions with him over banquets and during the conference, as well as there were other "informal discussions" with him during the course of the forum, as with other ministers too. "In general, there were also meetings between ministers and heads of delegations, as the aim of this (multilateral) forum is to exchange views, so there were many meetings, and a lot of things were discussed," the culture secretary said. SCO Forum's Indraprastha Communique calls for respecting every civilisation, heritage protection However, he didn't specify how many bilateral talks took place during the course of the Forum hosted by India from November 20-22. Asked if any bilateral meeting took place with Iran, he said, "There was a bilateral meeting with Iran. And India is in constant touch with Iran, and on areas in which there can be any cultural exchange, we are always in discussion. And discussions took place during the Summit too." The secretary said that during the bilateral meeting, "ideas have been thrown, though no such project has been concretised yet. But the discussions and engagements are on". The three-day event was hosted by the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of External Affairs. The Iranian Embassy in India in a post on X on Sunday said, at the civilisational summit, Tehran proposed setting up an "SCO Joint Network for Written Heritage and Civilisational Memory". Dr Faridoddin Faridasr, Cultural Counsellor of the Islamic Republic of Iran in India, addressed the First SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi, highlighting the importance of shared civilisational heritage as a foundation for cultural cooperation and mutual understanding among SCO member states, it said. In his remarks, he emphasised the historical role of the "Persian language as a language of science, literature, administration and cultural exchange across Central Asia, the Indian subcontinent and neighbouring regions, describing it as an important part of the shared cultural and historical heritage of the region". Referring to Iran's successful cultural cooperation with India, he highlighted the activities of the Noor International Microfilm Centre, affiliated with the Embassy of the Islamic Republic of Iran in New Delhi. Since 1990, the Centre has collaborated with 72 academic and cultural institutions in India, resulting in the digitisation of "more than 150,000 Persian and Arabic manuscripts," the restoration and preservation of over three million pages of historical documents, and the preparation of nearly 300 catalogues, the embassy said. Faridasr also referred to the ongoing joint projects with cultural institutions in Telangana and Hyderabad for the digitisation, restoration and preservation of historical Persian documents and manuscripts. As a practical initiative to strengthen regional cultural cooperation, he proposed the establishment of an "SCO Joint Network for Written Heritage and Civilizational Memory." "The proposed network would focus on the preservation and digitisation of manuscripts and historical documents, the exchange of technical expertise and training in manuscript restoration, and the promotion of shared linguistic and literary heritage through joint research, publications and exhibitions," the embassy said in a detailed post on X. He reaffirmed Iran's "readiness to share its experience and technical expertise with other SCO member states", stressing that the preservation of shared civilisational heritage provides an important opportunity to strengthen mutual trust, cultural understanding and cooperation across the region. The forum was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on November 20. It saw the participation of delegates from various Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) member countries, including Pakistan, and other countries.

articles.summary: Washington: The US is seeking answers from Nvidia on its chip sales to China and will find out who was in charge of compliance at the company formerly led by Jensen Huang, who resigned following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday. "We've been in touch with the temporary management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers, and we do need answers.... It behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was," Bessent told the CBS program "Face the Nation." Reports about Huang's relationship with a woman whom US intelligence suspects of being ​a Chinese spy and his extramarital affair with a company executive led to his resignation and investigations by US regulators and the FBI, congressional action, an internal review and a proposed investor class-action lawsuit. China’s spies set sights on AI chips years before Nvidia scandal Days after Huang's resignation, President Donald Trump's administration issued a rule to further restrict China's access to advanced AI chips from companies like Nvidia, tightening controls ahead of Trump's trip to China last week for talks with President Xi Jinping. Bessent said the chipmaker's board of directors is working to determine what had happened, and he expressed confidence that it would "come up with some very fulsome and robust answers." "We do need to see who was in charge of compliance there," Bessent said. "We will see which level of the business knew about this. Was it at the lower levels? Was it at the middle level? Did it go all the way to the top?" Trump said on Friday that he would like to see Huang apologize and return to Nvidia. Asked whether he agreed with Trump, Bessent said more information is needed. "I think we have to see where the buck stops," Bessent said. Nvidia board Chairman Harvey Jones has said the board will not rehire Huang.

articles.title: Mamata TMC files police complaint alleging fabrication of affidavits by rival faction
articles.summary: Kolkata: The Mamata TMC has lodged a police complaint alleging that the breakaway Democratic TMC, with the help of police personnel, fabricated affidavits to bolster its claim over the party's name and election symbol before the Election Commission. Mamata TMC treasurer Subhasish Chakraborty, a former MP, filed the complaint at Kalighat police station in Kolkata on November 20, naming Democratic TMC chairman Arup Roy and Leader of the Opposition Ritabrata Banerjee. Several personnel of the Nanoor police station in Birbhum district have also been named in the complaint. Mamata-led Trinamool Congress submits affidavits to Election Commission, Kalyan Banerjee accuses rival group of forgery The complaint comes amid a dispute over the party's leadership and identity following its split after the TMC lost the Assembly elections to the BJP earlier this year. Led by Ritabrata Banerjee , the breakaway group has claimed to be the genuine TMC, asserting that former chief minister Mamata Banerjee is no longer the party chairperson and that Howrah Madhya MLA Arup Roy holds the post. The dispute is pending before the EC, and both factions have submitted affidavits from party workers and elected representatives to establish their support. In the complaint, Chakraborty claimed that evidence in his possession pointed to an organised effort to prepare fake affidavits for the breakaway faction using the police machinery. According to the complaint, the alleged exercise took place between October 23 and 27, when personnel and civic volunteers of the Nanoor police station collected details of people from electoral rolls of nearby villages and filled them into pre-prepared affidavit formats. The complainant alleged that the affidavits were prepared in the names of people who had neither appeared before those drafting them nor authorised anyone to sign on their behalf. Their signatures were allegedly forged. The affidavits purportedly stated that the individuals concerned had nominated Roy as the leader of the All India Trinamool Congress and did not accept Mamata Banerjee as the party's leader, the complaint alleged. Chakraborty claimed that the aim was to create an artificial record of support for the breakaway faction in the proceedings before the EC. He said he was willing to provide evidence and documents to the police. Responses from the accused leaders and police were not immediately available. CPI(M) leader Sujan Chakraborty called for a proper investigation into the allegations.

articles.title: Uttar Pradesh BJP chief reiterates party's commitment to 'Radhe Radhe, Kamal Khila De' chant
articles.summary: Lucknow: Uttar Pradesh BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary on Sunday reiterated the party's commitment to the 'Radhe Radhe, Kamal Khila De' chant raised by the party during its recent Mathura meet and slammed the Samajwadi Party for raising objections to it. Chaudhary, also the Union Minister of State for Finance, said, "We are the followers of Sanatan Dharma. The 'Radhe-Radhe' chant is an expression of our inherent faith and culture. It is beyond comprehension why anyone would object to it." Chaudhary was referring to remarks made by SP chief Akhilesh Yadav that the BJP needed to invoke 'Radhe Radhe' as the lotus (BJP's election symbol) was "wilting". 'Radhe Radhe, Kamal Khila De': Lord Krishna takes centre stage as BJP gears up for 2027 UP elections Addressing a press conference in Lucknow after the BJP's Mathura meet, Yadav had said, "'Radhe Radhe Kamal Khila De' - Does it mean the lotus has wilted?" Samajwadi Party Lok Sabha MP Dimple Yadav had also expressed similar views. Invoking its religious and ideological legacy, the BJP had on November 17 put Lord Krishna at the centre of its key organisational meeting in Mathura, raising the slogan "Radhe Radhe, Kamal Khila De" and renewing its demand for a grand temple at the deity's birthplace as it geared up for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The political messaging from Mathura, associated with Lord Krishna, came as BJP national president Nitin Nabin, who attended the meeting, expressed confidence that the party would return to power in Uttar Pradesh for a third consecutive term, while Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya renewed the temple pitch with the slogan, "Ayodhya hui hamari hai, ab Mathura ki baari hai (Ayodhya has become ours; now it's Mathura's turn)." articles.title: Baiju Raju’s death: Distress and suicide can’t be reduced to a superficial ‘gender war’
articles.summary: On March 22, Baiju Raju, a 40-year-old Malayali man working in New Zealand, uploaded two videos multiple times on his YouTube channel. One of them is 19 minutes long, a discomfiting confrontation of his wife. In the video, Baiju is asking his wife to sit on a small stool, the camera trained on her as he questions her about an alleged affair. The second video, 10 minutes long, features a heartbroken Baiju declaring his anger towards his wife and her family for her infidelity. He is planning to take his own life, he says. A day after the videos were uploaded, Baiju was found dead in a lodge at his hometown of Kayamkulam in Kerala’s Alappuzha. In the hours that followed, Baiju’s videos quickly went viral. Immediate opinions were formed and narratives were woven, mostly of two kinds. A majority questioned and abused Baiju’s wife, claiming she pushed her husband to suicide. Others accused Baiju of being a toxic husband who left his wife with no option but to seek comfort elsewhere. Social media discourse has reduced a deeply personal tragedy — and a serious social issue of how dominant systems and structures can take people’s lives — into a no-nuance narrative of 'men’s rights vs feminism’. Can a partner’s actions distress a person enough to make them question their existence? Yes. Does it mean a woman in a heteronormative marriage should not make choices — whether ‘right’ or ‘wrong’ — for herself? No. In a patriarchy that has hard boundaries for what a husband and wife should be, and judges people for ‘failure’ to live up to these norms, can we reduce suicide to the consequences of another person’s actions? Definitely not. In this case, Baiju’s videos have drawn anger from those who feel wronged by women choosing to be independent agents of their own life. In the days that followed the news of Baiju’s death, members of a local men’s rights activist group had taken it upon themselves to ensure that the funeral on March 26 went off smoothly. “Due to the misuse of women’s rights laws, many men have died by suicide. When we came to know about Baiju, we volunteered to ensure justice for him. We have also filed complaints with the police,” a representative of the group, Firoz, told the media. The foundation also alleged on their Facebook page that neither the government nor the media was covering the case because the person who died was a man, not a woman. It’s important however to note two things: suicide is not an individual problem, but oftentimes the result of trying to live in systems that oppress all of us — patriarchy, caste, capitalism, heteronormativity, fascism. Secondly, our moral distinctions of what is right and wrong (cheating, in this case) cannot mean that we blame a person who made choices for herself and accuse her of killing her husband. According to Baiju’s father Kochukunju Raju, the friction between Baiju and his wife began around one-and-a-half years into their marriage. He has admitted to the media that she had filed a domestic violence complaint against Baiju in New Zealand, but claimed it was a false charge. Baiju had raised a similar allegation in one of the videos he posted, in which he accused his wife of making false claims to separate him from their daughter. The New Zealand police had separated the couple after the complaint, Baiju’s father told media persons. “After that, she left with their daughter and came to Kerala without even informing Baiju. He was very depressed because of this,” he said. He added that the wife had filed a divorce notice against Baiju, which had also vexed the latter. Baiju, too, said in his video that his only hope in life was his daughter, who he alleged was snatched away from him. Meanwhile, Baiju’s wife, who hails from Elanthoor in Pathanamthitta, has reportedly returned to New Zealand. The police team investigating the incident is learnt to have recorded statements of both of their family members. So far, no one has been booked. This is all we know of the domestic violence allegations and the living arrangements of the family. With this, any attempt to weigh the trauma of domestic violence against the trauma of a father who had to be separated from his child will be irresponsible. Human beings are not cardboard cutouts, and an abusive husband can be a loving father. However, individual instances of deep personal tragedy should not be the focus of this discourse. He said, she did not Every assumption so far made about the relationship between Baiju and his wife is ultimately based on two videos — both made in seemingly emotionally charged circumstances, by a man who can no longer speak for himself. It is to be noted that neither Baiju’s wife nor her family members have spoken publicly about their version of the events yet. All we know is that she had, at one point, filed a domestic violence complaint against her husband while in New Zealand, the details of which we are still not privy to. We have no evidence to believe that the case was falsely foisted, as alleged by Baiju and his father. So does it all simply come down to the question of whom to believe, or side with? More importantly, who even are we to make this judgement call? Firstly, it is not as if there is a one-size-fits-all definition for infidelity. As the Indian law doesn’t recognise adultery as a crime anymore, the understanding of what constitutes ‘cheating’ now almost exclusively depends on individual moral codes, which can change vastly from person to person, relationship to relationship. This personal sense of morality, in turn, is in a constant tussle with the Indian society at large — one that places the sanctity of marriage above all, relegating the man in the family to the role of a ‘provider and protector.’ Not fulfilling this role, and a hundred other things including the infidelity of a wife, leads to people questioning a man's masculinity, causing distress. As feminism and the fight for women's rights gain traction, a number of women are trying to break out of the roles set for them by patriarchy and choose their own paths. Several men however are not equipped to handle this renegotiation of gender roles in relationships and in society. Patriarchy puts the cisgender heterosexual man at the top of the gender hierarchy. Feminism says all genders are equal. But many cis-het men view equality and equity as them 'losing' power to women — and movements like men's rights activism drum up these fears further. In a country where up to 55% of married people have reportedly been unfaithful to their partners at least once (as per a survey conducted by ‘extramarital’ dating app Gleeden), the divorce rate is less than 1% , the lowest in the world. It is no secret that a significant number of couples in India are forced to stay in unhappy marriages for reasons ranging from religious ideals and societal reputation to ‘for the sake of the children.’ We still hold on to the outdated ideal of a long-lasting family unit over happiness. Baiju’s father said that he had told his son many times to leave his wife. “I asked him to take custody of the child and let his wife live her life, so he could also have a good family life. But he was not convinced,” he told the media. A man reduced to his heartbreak The mainstream narrative surrounding Baiju’s death, formed exclusively based on the fact that he was found dead hours after he uploaded videos accusing his wife of infidelity, is easy and reductive — a heartbroken husband dies by suicide after finding out about his wife’s affair. This has also led to criticism of Baiju’s decision, with many questioning if an act of infidelity indeed warranted such a reaction. Why did he not think of his daughter, some ask. But it has to be noted that even though Baiju had uploaded these two videos together, neither of them was made immediately prior to his death. In fact, both the videos were filmed in New Zealand, with the ‘confrontation’ supposedly having taken place in May last year. It is not known exactly when the second video was shot. The fact is, we don’t know what happened in the time between when the first video was shot and when Baiju was found dead. What had happened in New Zealand after his wife filed a domestic violence complaint against him? Were there any conversations between the couple after that? Did he have a healthy social support system to help him through the break-up? Did his support system provide him with resources to help with his mental health? That is the conversation we should be having — about taking our mental health seriously, about providing accessible support for everyone, about not shaming people for reaching out for help. We should be talking about how to support our friends and family better — whether they're suffering domestic violence or heartbreak. We should be talking about the complexities of human suffering. Reducing everything to a binary is not only unhelpful, it's actively harmful. Views expressed are the authors' own.
